content.content:
#### Wrap

The Wrap button, with a wrap-text icon, turns soft wrapping on and off, showing as selected while it is on. Its tooltip says whether long lines wrap or run past the edge, and that clicking does the other, with its shortcut, Alt+Z. It starts off. While it is on, a line longer than the editor is wide wraps at the editor's right edge, at a space where there is one and mid-word where there isn't, onto as many visual rows as it needs, each row after the first starting at the line's own indentation, so the text never scrolls sideways and the horizontal scrollbar goes. Only how the text shows changes: the file's text, its line numbers, the language server's positions, and what is saved are the same either way, and Home, End, and selecting by line act on visual rows while on, as in other editors, Home's smart indentation applying to the line's first row. The ruler and its shade stay at the 80th column, wrapped or not. Turning it on or off keeps the cursor's line in view where it was. The choice is remembered for the user, as the [UserPreferencesScope](../user-preferences/index.md#user-preferences-scope) says, the same for every file and project, and holds for every file opened after.

    wrap:
        The Wrap button, with a wrap-text icon, hard wraps the text at 80
        columns, the ruler's, by Piton's rules, changing the file's text
        itself, as `piton format` changes it. It is an action, not a mode:
        clicking it, or pressing Alt+Z, wraps once, and the editor never
        wraps as it is typed in, nor shows a line any other way than as it
        is. It wraps the lines the selection touches, or, with nothing
        selected, the whole file. Its tooltip says it wraps long lines at 80
        columns, with its shortcut. It is shown only for a Piton file, and
        is disabled while the file can't be edited yet.

        Wrapping never changes what the file says: the file compiles to
        exactly what it did before, and only lines past the 80th column are
        touched. A line is broken only where Piton joins it back as it was,
        so each break is at a single space, which the break takes the place
        of, in the prose of a multi-line value, the lines after it taking
        the indentation of the line broken, as consecutive lines of a
        string block join with one space. Short lines are never joined, and
        a paragraph is never reflowed: only lines that run long are split,
        each at the last space it may break at before the 80th column, or,
        where there is none, at the first after it.

        Nothing is broken where Piton would read it otherwise. A line is
        never broken inside an expression in braces, whether written plain
        or after a dollar sign, a hash, or an at sign, nor inside an escape
        wrapper, nor at all inside an escape block or a code fence, whose
        text is kept exactly. No break is made where the line it starts
        would begin with `- `, `+ `, or `++ `, which make a list item or a
        composition line, with `//`, which makes a comment, with a
        backslash, or with a word followed by a colon and a space, which
        makes a key; the break moves to the space before or after instead.
        A line holding a key and its value, `name: value`, a list item, an
        import, or a declaration is never broken, since what follows it
        indented would be something else. A comment that runs long is
        broken the same way, its later lines comments of their own, each
        begun with `// ` at its indentation. A line with nowhere it may be
        broken is left as it is, however long.

        The wrap is one edit, undone in one step, and keeps the cursor and
        the selection on the same text. A file the language server reports
        errors in still wraps, by the same rules. Wrapping doesn't save the
        file; saving it formats it as ever.

EOF
tail -n +$e $f >> /tmp/x; cp /tmp/x $f
perl -0pi -e 's/the Wrap and close buttons icon buttons/the Wrap and close buttons icon buttons/' $f
g=spec/scope/user-preferences/index.pi; grep -v "whether the editor wraps long lines" $g > /tmp/y; cp /tmp/y $g; grep -n "EditorScope" $g

content.text:
The editor's Wrap is now a hard wrap at 80 columns by Piton's rules, replacing the soft-wrap toggle. `piton check` reports no problems and `piton build` wrote 82 files.

- **How it works:** Wrap (or Alt+Z) is a one-off action that rewrites the file's text. It never wraps as you type. It wraps the selected lines, or the whole file when nothing is selected, and only appears for Piton files.
- **Never changes meaning:** the file must compile to exactly what it did before.
  - Only lines past column 80 are split, each at a single space, and the new line takes the broken line's indentation. Short lines are never joined.
  - Nothing is broken inside an expression, an escape wrapper, an escape block or a code fence.
  - A break never starts a line that Piton would read differently: one beginning with `- `, `+ `, `++ `, `//`, a backslash, or `word: `.
  - Lines holding a key and its value, list items, imports and declarations are never broken.
  - Long comments become several `// ` lines.
  - A line with nowhere safe to break is left as it is.
- **Editing:** one wrap is one undo step. The cursor and selection stay on the same text. Wrapping doesn't save the file.
- **Preference removed:** the remembered wrap setting is gone from `UserPreferencesScope`, since there's no longer a mode to remember.

**Anchors the code should follow:** `EditorScope` `#wrap` and `#layout`, and `UserPreferencesScope`, where the old preference was removed.

**Anchors the code should follow:** `EditorScope` `#wrap` and `#layout`, and `UserPreferencesScope`, where the old preference was removed.
